english: Grandmother, tell me a story of an oath. Two brothers made an oath at the ford. The first said: I will guard your herd. But at night he drove the herd away, and he sold it. What did the river do? The river seized the first one at the ford, and he sank. And the other one? The other found his own herd, and he rejoiced. Will you keep your oaths, child? I will keep them, grandmother.

english: Host, you fed me at your fire. You are a giver of good things. You are dear to me, guest. Let us set a pledge between us. What pledge? This knife of my father's. Will you take it, and give me your cup? I give you my cup, and our kin will be friends. May the gods hear this pledge.

english: Mistress, give me your swift horse. I will bring him back at the new moon. What pledge will you give me? I will give you my father's cup. Is that cup worth a horse? It is worth two horses. Then bring the cup in the morning. If you do not bring the swift one back, I will take the cup. I vow it to you, mistress.

english: The Sheep and the Horses

english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

english: Shepherd, three of my goats are gone. Did you sell them at the ford? I did not sell them, master. A wolf devoured them; look at their blood in the grass. And where were you? I was driving the other goats to the water. Will you show me the wolf's tracks? I will show them to you. Will you go there now? I will go. If the tracks are there, you owe me nothing.

english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

english: Mother, the elders gave our field to Of-Good-Fame. They did not show what is right. Why are you angry, son? They are wise men. But my grandfather ploughed that field. And your grandfather sold it to the father of Of-Good-Fame. I was there, and I know it. Then I will not be angry. But my heart is heavy. Come, and eat meat with me.

pie: kʷíd h₁wésuḱlewes h₂réh₁dʰesi? h₂yuHn̥ḱós poh₂imḗn uksénm̥ stéh₂yet? h₁ím ne stéh₂yet. uksḗn gʰórdʰom Hrunépt dóruh₂-kʷe h₁n̥dó bʰéwgt. kʷíh₁ tód wóydth₂e? gʰórdʰom dedórḱh₂e. uksnés-kʷe pédās réh₁tm̥. nu h₃reǵtóm déyḱsomes poh₂imḗn h₁léwdʰeros. uksnés-kʷe gʰóstipotis h₁ím drúsu h₂isḱétu. h₁ésmey ḱód wéwkēsi?
english: Of-Goodly-Fame, what do you counsel? Did the young herdsman steal the bull? He did not steal it. The bull broke the fence and fled into the woods. How do you know it? I have seen the fence. And I found the bull's tracks. Then let us show what is right: the herdsman is free. And let the master of the bull seek it in the woods. Will you tell him this?

pie: wóyḱe dʰh₁tléh₂ dʰǵʰyés wéwket. kʷóti toy gʷṓs dʰl̥gʰóh₂? déḱm̥ gʷṓs uksénm̥-kʷe. tód moy uksnés h₂elgʷʰós. h₂elgʷʰós gʷr̥dús. nu toy pénkʷe gʷṓs gʰéldʰōh₂ pénkʷe-kʷe h₂élyās sh₁séni gʰéldʰōh₂. tód h₃m̥néh₃esi? ph₂térm̥ dyḗm h₃m̥néh₃mi. nu toy wékʷos h₁áyh₂e. sh₁ésonm̥ mē mérs.
english: Neighbour, the assembly spoke yesterday. How many cows do I owe you? Ten cows and a bull. That is the price of my bull. The price is heavy. Now I will pay you five cows, and five others at harvest time. Will you swear to it? I swear by Father Sky. Then I accept your word. But do not forget the harvest time!

english: Husband, why are you trembling? I swore a lie in the assembly. What did you say? I said: I did not take our neighbour's calf. But I did take it, and I hid it in our enclosure. The gods have seen it! Sky sees all things. I am afraid of him. What shall I do, wife? Give the calf back, and pay the penalty. Then may the gods be kindly to you.

english: Father-in-law, I bring you cattle and a cauldron for your daughter. Your cattle are good. But will you guard my daughter and love her? I will guard her, and I will love her. I give you my word as a pledge. Then you are my son-in-law. Come and drink with me. And when will I lead your daughter to my house? At the new moon.

english: Brother of the dead man, I bring you the blood-price, a hundred cows. Will they give my brother back to me? He lies in the earth. They will not give him back. But there will be no killing between our houses. My mother weeps at night. What shall I say to her? Say: the slayer has paid, and Sky has seen it. Then I accept the cattle, and I will not take vengeance.

english: Master, the summer has gone; give me my wage. What did I tell you? You told me: I will give you a foal and a lamb. But you slept in the grass, and a wolf carried off a lamb. And I worked for you the whole summer. You speak boldly, orphan. Take the foal, and leave me the lamb. Give me that one too, or I will go to the king. Then take it, bold one!

english: Chief, my husband's brother owes you three foals. He went away across the ford, and he has not come. Then who will pay his debt? I give you my loom as a pledge. A loom is not worth three foals. I will also weave wool for your daughters in the winter. If he comes home safe, let him pay me the debt himself. Will you keep this pledge, woman? I will keep it, chief, and may Dawn see it.

english: Mother-in-law, my hands are trembling. At dawn I will stand before the women of the village. Did you take the gold? I did not take it, mother-in-law. Then why do you tremble? What is true does not fear. The women do not trust me. I trust you, and I will stand beside you. Look at the sun, and speak true words.

english: Father, Of-Good-Horses and Of-True-Fame want this calf. Which of the two speaks the truth? Let the calf go, and watch. The calf will run to its own mother. It ran to the cow of Of-Good-Horses! Then Of-Good-Horses will lead it home. Do you see, son? A cow does not lie. And Of-True-Fame? Will the elders punish him? His lie will cost him a sheep.

english: Do not kill me, master! Why were you in my enclosure at night? I was hungry. My children are hungry. Did you take anything? I took nothing. Then sit down by my fire and eat. But in the morning you will work in my field. I will work, and I will not steal again.

english: Uncle, how do I say this before the assembly? I did not steal the horse. Say: I did not steal the horse. Does your heart tremble? My heart trembles, uncle. Speak slowly, and do not be silent. A man who speaks the truth does not fear.

pie: ḱéywa gʷḗn h₂egʷnóns bʰéroh₂ h₁yóns toy dʰl̥gʰóh₂. kʷóti h₁sénti? oḱtṓw h₂egʷnṓs moysós-kʷe. dʰl̥gʰós septḿ̥ h₂egʷnṓs h₁ést. moysóm toy éti h₁opéyoh₂ h₁yód h₁eǵóh₂ gʷr̥dús h₁ésm̥. wékʷos toy h₁sn̥tyóm túH-kʷe moy ḱéywos. ḱósmi nos wékʷsperoy ph₂wéni h₁édesi? h₁édoh₂ pótnih₂m-kʷe moy wédʰōh₂.
english: Dear woman, I bring the lambs that I owe you. How many are there? Eight lambs and a ram. The debt was seven lambs. I give you the ram too, because I was slow. Your word is true, and you are dear to me. Will you eat at our fire this evening? I will eat, and I will bring my wife.

pie: ǵń̥h₃ra deḱsiwóm h₁mé méne-kʷe swēḱuróm h₁entér déyḱsdʰi. kʷíd dʰéh₁t? h₁ésmey moy kʷérom h₁opéyom h₁ím-kʷe Hrunépt. kʷíh₁ h₁ím Hrunépt? h₁ím h₂éḱmonn̥s h₁épi Hyéh₁kt. nu toy kʷérom káprom-kʷe dʰl̥gʰéti. h₁íns toy ǵʰiméns pró gʰéldʰetu. wékʷesh₂ toy h₁wésuh₂.
english: Wise woman, show what is proper between me and my brother-in-law. What did he do? I gave him my cauldron, and he broke it. How did he break it? He threw it onto the stones. Then he owes you a cauldron and a goat. Let him pay them to you before the winter. Your words are good.

pie: kʷíd toy gʷḗn ḱóymosyo h₂néres bʰréy dʰédʰh₁n̥ti? h₁yós káprom stéh₂yēti só tríns káprons dédeh₃tu. h₁yós-kʷe súHm̥ h₁r̥h₁pyḗti só dwóh₁ súHh₁e dédeh₃tu. h₁yód ne kʷinéwonti kʷíd dʰédʰh₁n̥ti? nu káprosyo wiḱpóteyey wr̥ǵyéti. ḱéh₂ wékʷesh₂ gʷr̥dúh₂. kʷoynéh₂ usméy médʰi méǵyōs? bʰṓr n̥sméy médʰi dwís kʷinéwti.
english: Woman, what do the men of your village do to a thief? Whoever steals a goat, let him give three goats. And whoever carries off a pig, let him give two pigs. If he does not pay, what do they do? Then he works for the master of the goat. These are heavy words. Is the penalty greater among your people? Among us the thief pays twice.

pie: méh₂ter h₃rḗǵs septḿ̥ pṓlHons n̥sméd h₂epó gʷʰédʰyeti. kʷíd h₁íns gʷʰédʰyeti? h₂nérm̥ dh₂pnóy stunédm̥ h₁ím ne moréyom. kʷíd h₁ím stunéds? sékʷt ph₂tḗr toy bʰṓr. nu h₁éy kʷoynéh₂m éti dʰl̥gʰṓh₂. septḿ̥ pṓlHons kʷinéwomes. h₃rḗǵs h₃reǵtóm ne déyḱeti. ḱód mē h₂éǵs. polh₁éwes ǵʰoysṓs h₃rēǵéy h₁sénti.
english: Mother, the king asks us for seven foals. Why does he ask for them? I struck a man at the feast, but I did not kill him. Why did you strike him? He said: your father is a thief. Then he too will owe a penalty. But we will pay the seven foals. The king does not show what is right. Do not say this! The king has many spears.

english: Do you hear that? Someone is in the cow-stall. I hear it. Be silent! Do you see? A young man is leading a foal out of the stall. Shall we seize him? He holds a spear; let us follow him. At dawn we will tell the elders what we have seen. Will they trust us? They will trust us, because we speak what is true.

pie: h₁súḱlewes h₃rḗǵs h₁mé ḱóymōd h₁éǵʰs h₁élh₂t. kʷíd te h₃rḗǵs h₁éǵʰs h₁élh₂t? dusménesm̥ kh₃téwi gʷʰénm̥. h₁éy ǵʰoysóh₁ h₁mé próti gʷémt. tód kʷis ne dedórḱe? tód kʷis ne dedórḱe h₃rḗǵs-kʷe h₁mé h₃eh₃óde. h₁ésyo ǵnéh₃meh₂m h₃eh₃ódh₂e. kúdʰe príHe h₁éyomes? h₂éwh₂om moy h₁éyomes. nu te sékʷōh₂er téḱneh₂-kʷe nos éti sékʷētor.
english: Of-Good-Fame, the king drove me out of the village. Why did the king drive you out? I killed Ill-Minded in a fight. He came at me with a spear. Has no one seen it? No one has seen it, and the king hates me. I hate his judgment. Where shall we go, dear one? We will go to my mother's brother. Then I will follow you, and our children will follow too.

pie: kʷíd h₂énHe h₁óytos? h₁óytos wékʷos mórtos deywóybʰos h₁yód mléwHti. h₁íd ḱlush₁yónti h₁íd-kʷe memnḗr. kʷíd wiHrṓy dʰédʰh₁n̥ti h₁yós dʰrugʰyéti? h₁ím kʷéyonti. h₁ésyo péḱu néḱt h₁ésyo-kʷe suHnéwes péh₂urōs. téḱnom toy ph₂térm̥ dʰrugʰyḗsi? h₂énHe h₁ím ne dʰrugʰyṓh₂. deywóybʰos dedwóyh₂e. nu toy dyḗws h₂óyu déh₃eti.
english: Grandmother, what is an oath? An oath is a word which a man says to the gods. They hear it, and they remember it. What do they do to the man who deceives? They punish him. His cattle are lost, and his sons are few. Will you deceive your father, child? I will not deceive him, grandmother. I fear the gods. Then Sky will give you a long life.

pie: swéḱruh₂ moy ǵl̥h₂ṓws méne h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m lémbʰt. kʷíd h₁íh₂m̥ lémbʰt? wérh₁yeti h₁íh₂m̥ snéh₁m̥. kʷótereh₂ h₁íh₂m̥ snéh₁t? h₁íh₂m̥ snéh₁m̥ h₁yénh₂tēr-kʷe moy h₁mé widét. nu h₁íh₂m̥ préḱsoh₂. h₁yód ḱód éti wérh₁yēti téwe toy ǵl̥h₂ṓws h₁íh₂m̥ h₂éti déh₃eti. gʰrémēti-kʷe moy? gʰrémetu h₁sn̥tyóm bʰh₂énti.
english: Mother-in-law, my husband's sister took my wool. Why did she take it? She says: I spun it. Which of you two spun it? I spun it, and my husband's brother's wife saw me. Then I will ask her. If she says this too, your husband's sister will give it back to you. And will she be angry with me? Let her be angry; you speak what is true.
